takeaways: Office distress sets new records: office CMBS special servicing hit 15.7% (13.2% delinquent), and Philadelphia's Centre Square sold for $70M against a $471M 2019 appraisal, wiping out seven tranches and producing a rare AAA loss.

Capital is still hunting discounted office: L&L Infinite paid $245M ($425/SF) for 600 Third Ave on a $215M Bain Capital loan, and Deloitte finds nearly 80% of 950 CRE execs plan to reposition assets within 18 months.

The AI buildout is reshaping real estate: $10.3T of U.S. data center investment is projected through 2032 even as Oracle's New Mexico mega-project shows cracks, while DWS pitches housing as the 'AI immunity trade' with multifamily rent growth running through 2029.

items.headline: Office CMBS special servicing hits record 15.7%
items.summary: CRED iQ data covering $189.6B of office debt shows special servicing at a record 15.7% in August, with office delinquency at 13.2% versus 8.2% across all property types; conduit office is worst at 18.5%. CRED iQ says 71% of distressed office balance reflects failed or imminent refinancings rather than missed payments, and $13.9B of the $39B maturing in the next 12 months already shows warning signs.

items.headline: Philly's Centre Square sells for $70M, 85% below 2019 value
items.summary: The twin-tower Centre Square office complex at 1500 Market St. sold for $70M versus a $471M appraisal in 2019, wiping out seven lower CMBS tranches and marking only the third AAA-level loss since the financial crisis; Pimco faces a loss of more than $35M. Occupancy had collapsed to 28% from 93%, and buyers PMC Property Group and Dean Adler plan a 300-room hotel and up to 500 apartments.

items.headline: Ex-Silverstein CEO Marty Burger's L&L Infinite buys 600 Third for $245M
items.summary: L&L Infinite, Marty Burger's new JV with L&L principal David Levinson, paid $245M ($425/SF) for the 92%-leased Manhattan tower at 600 Third Ave, financed with a $215M Bain Capital loan and brokered by Newmark, with Mack Real Estate, BLDG and BD Blakely co-investing. Deals where one principal stays in with new partners and a fresh capital stack are on the rise. (via The Promote)

items.headline: AI data center boom: $10.3T of U.S. investment projected through 2032
items.summary: U.S. data center and AI infrastructure investment is projected at $10.3T from 2025 to 2032 (about 3.6% of GDP a year), with Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle expected to spend $4.2T in capex through 2029, increasingly debt-financed. Private data center construction hit $37B through July, up about $9B year-over-year, pulling labor and materials away from other construction, including housing.

items.headline: Deloitte: CRE heads into 2027 with capital to spend, selectively
items.summary: Deloitte's survey of 950 CRE executives finds 51% expect revenue growth above 5%, nearly 80% plan to upgrade or reposition assets within 12-18 months, and cross-border CRE investment rose 18% year-over-year in Q1. Over 90% plan to boost data and tech spending, but only 8% have integrated AI, and 59% of U.S. CRE leaders are within a decade of retirement.

items.headline: DWS's Todd Henderson: real estate is the 'AI immunity trade'
items.summary: DWS's Todd Henderson argues the roughly 25% peak-to-trough value reset was driven by discount rates, not failing fundamentals, and projects strong multifamily rent growth through 2029 as construction starts fall, especially in the Sun Belt. He also favors retail, where vacancy is at 25-year lows, and real estate debt, positioning hard assets as a hedge against AI disruption.

items.headline: Tribe buying Fairmont Scottsdale Princess for $650M+
items.summary: A Native American tribe is buying the Fairmont Scottsdale Princess resort in Scottsdale, Arizona for more than $650M, or roughly $900K per key, according to Green Street's Real Estate Alert. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Cracks appear in Oracle's massive New Mexico AI data center project
items.summary: The WSJ reports problems, including force-majeure issues, at Oracle's large AI data center build-out in New Mexico, a warning sign for the debt-financed hyperscaler capex wave that is reshaping industrial and land markets. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Facilo raises about $41M and acquires AI valuation firm Collavit
items.summary: Japanese brokerage platform Facilo, used by 13,000+ agents across 2,300 broker offices, raised a ¥6.4B (about $41M) Series B led by Globis Capital Partners and acquired AI appraisal firm Collavit. The company plans to launch an AI CRM and survey agent, part of the ongoing push to put AI into core brokerage and seller-side workflows.

items.headline: Blake Management Group pushes ahead with third-party growth strategy
items.summary: Senior living operator Blake Management Group is expanding its third-party management business, taking on communities for outside owners. The move reflects rising owner demand for experienced operators as senior housing occupancy recovers and new capital enters the sector.

items.headline: Airbnb's Brian Chesky spends three hours a day on hiring
items.summary: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky says he spends about three hours daily on recruiting and acts as co-hiring manager for his direct reports' hires, crediting Sam Altman's advice that hiring should be 50% of a CEO's job. He frames it as succession planning: an exec's direct reports are the likely successors, so leadership alignment has to run two levels deep.

items.headline: How boutique senior living operators compete against the giants
items.summary: Smaller senior living operators say a hands-on, high-touch operating model, with executives closely involved in each community, is how they win residents and owners against larger platforms. The piece is relevant for mid-size operators weighing scale against service quality.

items.headline: Clopen Capital wins planning for €115M Dublin senior living scheme
items.summary: Clopen Capital secured planning permission for a €115M senior and healthcare living development in Dublin, adding to growing institutional interest in purpose-built senior housing across Europe.

items.headline: Uber CEO: 'really demanding' culture includes weekend emails
items.summary: Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi says the company expects employees to answer emails on weekends and warns people who want to coast not to join, a blunt example of CEOs publicly raising performance expectations.

items.headline: Walmart offers Gen Z a path to six figures without a degree
items.summary: Walmart is offering job-training pathways into roles such as truck driver, technician and optician that can reach six-figure pay without a college degree. It's a model for operators competing for frontline talent in tight labor markets like senior living.

items.headline: Sleep predicts life expectancy better than diet or exercise
items.summary: OHSU researchers led by Andrew McHill found that getting less than seven hours of sleep a night was more strongly associated with county-level life expectancy than diet or physical inactivity; only smoking ranked higher. The observational study in Sleep Advances drew renewed attention this week.

items.headline: Heirless billionaire pours fortune into Texas ghost town of 25 people
items.summary: With no heirs to leave his wealth to, a billionaire is investing his fortune in reviving a tiny Texas town of about 25 residents, an unusual bet on rural placemaking and community building.
